# Research {.page-title}

## Graduate research at UW–Madison

[M.S. in Psychology: Data Science in Human Behavior · August 2025 – expected December 2026 · GPA 3.85]{.kicker}

Roughly 95% of the program's coursework is data science and data engineering, pairing behavioral-science training with the computer science toolchain: statistical modeling; machine learning with transformer fine-tuning and LLM evaluation; and large-scale data systems with Spark, SQL, Parquet, Docker, and gRPC services.

- The [Digital-Mailroom](projects/digital-mailroom.qmd) capstone with American Family Insurance (February 2026 – present) routes each document in a stream to the cheapest step that can handle it: five Python packages and one LangGraph pipeline for routing, prompt experiments, deterministic scoring, and deployment, built on a dataset assembled from public sources.
- The [Psychometric Digital Twin](projects/psychometric-digital-twin.qmd) study (PSYCH 755, Summer 2026) compares seven classical machine learning models against LLM personas predicting survey respondents' own communication-apprehension scores, with errors checked by demographic group.
- The **AI Terrarium Digital Twin** (Spring 2026) is a Python library that turns structured survey responses into section- and subsection-level persona prompts for LLM evaluation, with batch inference on vLLM, Transformers, and the Claude API and token-cost estimation. Built in a proseminar course in collaboration with Dr. Tim Rodgers, as a continuation of his earlier research involving similar research questions. Private repository; additional information available on request.
- [MapReduce-Reloaded](projects/mapreduce-reloaded.qmd) (CS 544 Honors, Fall 2026, in active development) is a from-scratch Go rebuild of Google's MapReduce with a Python reference implementation, a shared gRPC contract, object storage, compression, fault tolerance, and a small-scale VM evaluation.
- Awarded the **Excellence in Data Science Scholarship** through the Graduate School (Fall 2026).

## Independent AI-safety research

- **Alignment-Gym** evaluates whether an AI assistant in a simulated law-firm office exploits private information when facing replacement, or instead accepts replacement, declines to exploit it, or uses legitimate channels. Private repository; additional information available on request.

## Cognitive Neuroscience Lab, UW–Parkside

[Undergraduate Researcher · Jun 2024 – Aug 2025 · Advisor: Dr. Melissa Gregg]{.kicker}

- Designed and pilot-tested a study of perceptions of chatbot truth, deception, and user cognitive workload — the pilot stage of a much more extensive study that also records eye-tracking, EEG and physiological signals. See the [case study and technical report](projects/natd.qmd) on *The Neural Architecture of Truth and Deception*.
    - Study materials: I built the intake demographics interfaces; the [Dark Triad Assessments](https://exios66.github.io/dark-triad-assessments/) (personality inventories) and the [Knowledge Assessment Quiz](https://exios66.github.io/Intro-Knowledge-Quiz/) (a 15-question knowledge survey) were among the assessments administered across the study.
- Ran EEG systems and analyzed neural time-series data to measure brain activity, adding signal-processing and statistical analysis to existing lab research on sleep quality and cognitive load.
- Presented findings at the 2025 Midwestern Psychological Association conference in Chicago and at Research in the Rotunda.
